mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST is below its 12-month average for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS), signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress corporate profit margins and lead to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months AND PAYEMS monthly change < -0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE > 5% for three months and PAYEMS decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side slowdown, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below its 12-month average for four months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent increase in savings rate (proxied by RSAFS YoY growth > 3%) signals a shift to an accommodative policy regime, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS < 2% and RSAFS YoY growth > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 > 4% YoY growth) alongside rising housing starts (HOUST > 10% above 12-month average) signals robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 4% AND HOUST > 10% above 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 YoY > 4% and HOUST is above its 12-month average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) combined with accelerating wage growth (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly for three months) signals a tight labor market, which increases input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS monthly growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly growth for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a robust supply recovery, which improves corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above its 12-month average for six months but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10).
